title_candidates: OpenAI's Admin plugin puts workspace controls in a chat
A safer first test for OpenAI's new Admin plugin
summary: OpenAI's Admin plugin brings usage, access, and supported workspace actions into ChatGPT Work and Codex. Start with a read-only admin pilot.

primary_source.title: Introducing the Admin plugin for ChatGPT Work and Codex
primary_source.author: OpenAI
key_facts: The Admin plugin lets workspace administrators inspect information, change supported settings, and confirm authorized actions from a conversation in ChatGPT Work or Codex.

Supported tasks include reviewing adoption and credit usage, managing members and groups, diagnosing permission problems, controlling model or feature access, and handling usage limits and spending requests.
Admins can automate recurring checks and high-volume requests, including sending pending usage requests to Slack or Microsoft Teams and granting feature access when predefined criteria are met.

The plugin preserves each administrator's existing role and permissions, maps instructions to supported read or write actions, returns structured results, and allows broader-impact changes to be reviewed before application.
For ChatGPT Work, OpenAI says administrators first enable the plugin in workspace settings and then install it from the Plugins directory in the web or desktop app.

quote_candidates.text: The Admin plugin works within each user's existing role and permissions; it does not grant broader access.
quote_candidates.position: Scale administration with existing controls section

supporting_sources.title: Plugins in ChatGPT and Codex
key_facts: Workspace admins manage plugin installation in Workspace settings under Plugins and configure underlying app access and permissions under Apps.
A plugin inherits the access, action, confirmation, and source-system permissions of any app it uses.
OpenAI recommends a limited pilot, read-only access where possible, confirmation for sensitive actions, and privacy or legal review before broader rollout.
After installation, users can invoke a plugin with an @ mention or from the More menu in ChatGPT.

supporting_sources.title: Global Admin Console
key_facts: Eligible ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, and Edu organizations can use the Global Admin Console for identity and access, analytics, billing where available, and governance.
Workspace admins and owners see only the workspaces and actions allowed by their role; selecting another resource does not add permissions.
Available analytics can include active users, messages, credit use, tokens, Codex activity, plugin calls, and skill usage.
Authorized admins can review supported administrative events in searchable audit logs.

prerequisites: An eligible managed ChatGPT workspace where the Admin plugin is available
A non-sensitive, read-only question about your own workspace

steps.instruction: Open Workspace settings > Plugins, select Admin, and review its included capabilities and required apps; stop if the plugin is absent or your role cannot approve it.

Limit the first rollout to an administrator pilot role, keep app access read-only where possible, and require confirmation for write actions; pause for privacy, security, legal, or data-residency review if sensitive systems are involved.
Make the plugin available to that pilot role, then open the Plugin Directory in ChatGPT Work, search for Admin, and install it; stop if the listing or Connect control is unavailable.
Start a new ChatGPT Work conversation, invoke @Admin or choose + > More > Admin, and ask it to show aggregate ChatGPT Work and Codex activity for the last seven days without making changes.

Check that the result is limited to workspaces and data your role can already access, then review the admin audit log; do not test member, group, limit, or spending changes unless the displayed confirmation exactly matches an authorized request.

risk_flags: Availability depends on the workspace plan, role, region, surface, and plugin or app settings.
The guide uses a narrow administrator pilot and read-only questions before any write action.
The Admin plugin preserves existing permissions; readers should stop if returned data or requested scope exceeds their role.
The announcement describes Slack and Microsoft Teams automations, but the guide does not ask readers to configure them because that needs broader organizational review.
